artifact: skills/adversarial-review/SKILL.md - the evidence standards
finding: The both-polarity probe binds a guard under review but is nowhere stated to bind a finding's own proposed remedy; three remedies in PR #232's review (round one's M5, cycle one's P1 and P3) diagnosed correctly and prescribed a change that would have reddened lawful work, each caught only because the defense ran the counterfactual unprompted.
promotion: a remedy that lands unprobed in the lawful polarity, or a cycle where the defense does not run the counterfactual and a fix reddens a lawful call.

artifact: tools/lint.py - _redirected's crediting of check_output's implicit stdout
finding: The guard credits check_output's implicit stdout and also reads an explicit stdout= keyword on it, so check_output(cmd, stdin=DEVNULL, stdout=PIPE, stderr=DEVNULL) scores three covered streams and passes clean while the call raises ValueError('stdout argument not allowed') on every execution -- the spelling the shipped reference calls impossible. The remedy is determined (a launcher in _IMPLICIT that names the stream it owns is reported as an invalid call rather than as a partial redirect) but needs its own finding class, message and pin, against a failure that is deterministic and self-naming on first run.
promotion: a check_output call naming stdout reaching a branch, or a session reporting that lint passed a call that raises ValueError.

artifact: tools/roster.py — matches(), and the mutation pins on it in tools/tests/test_roster.py
finding: Two mutants of the predicate survive the whole suite and are left unpinned: normalising then .strip() on both sides, and normalising then .lower(). Each is behaviour-changing - an entry differing from its cell only in leading or trailing whitespace, or only in the case of one description word, fires under the shipped predicate and is forgiven under the mutant. Pinning every relaxation of a predicate nobody has proposed was judged unbounded work against a failure mode with no route into the tree, since the entry is generated from the cell and neither whitespace nor case drifts on its own.
promotion: a predicate normalising whitespace or case is proposed for matches() or written into a sibling normaliser this one is harmonised with, or an entry differing from its cell only in trailing whitespace or only in case reaches a tree.

artifact: skills/adversarial-review/references/after-the-fix.md — the post-fix look's scope
finding: The look on PR #231 ran under the pre-#230 scope and prosecuted the review's own bookkeeping. One of its seven findings was purely that: the PR body's mutation-matrix control row, which the defense then disproved - the published figure was correct, and fixing it would have replaced it with one no deterministic run produces. It cost a look, a defense verdict and a ruling to establish that nothing was wrong. A second finding counted revisions in two self-referential sentences and reads as bookkeeping, but its sites were in tracked files and it was fixed, so it is not an instance. #230 retired that scope after this review closed; this is one measured instance of what the retired clause produced, recorded rather than acted on because the clause is already gone.
promotion: a later post-fix look returns apparatus-facing findings again despite the retired scope, or the retirement is argued to have been reversed.

artifact: commit c830f51's message, PR #246
finding: States a derived comparison -- 'The surface is net smaller than at the base despite the grown authoring description' -- with no command and no tree. A commit message is named in both the figure rule's list and the behaviour rule's, so the falsifier (which command, on which tree?) applies and is unanswered. Sustained but not fixed: the only remedy is a history rewrite, and be0c943 is cited by the experience-session note, all five seat reports, the assignment, both defenses and both rulings, none of which can be repaired once orphaned. The one remedy on the docket that would destroy the review's own evidence base.
promotion: a correction path for a landed commit message that does not require rewriting history, or a second instance where the unverifiable figure actually misleads someone.

artifact: docs/architecture/decisions/README.md -- the claim-correcting repair's bounds
finding: Silent on whether the frozen archive D-53-D-69 is inside the permission, where the repoint permission answers the same question explicitly one paragraph above ('D-53-D-69 are inside this permission'). The conspicuous asymmetry reads as deliberate exclusion. Not ruled the owner's: undoing a wrong pick costs an edit to a repo-only README, not habit or what others saw, so it fails the fork test. Not fixed: the only remedy is added prose on a surface this change already grew, against a session meeting a falsified sentence in entries D-135 itself says 'nothing sends a reader there to act'.

artifact: tools/lint.py -- the decision-entry guards
finding: No check couples the [corrected] marker to its Erratum block. Probed on a git archive copy by two independent stages with in-class negative controls: a silent claim rewrite of a landed entry, a marker with no block, a block with no marker (the footer-only shape the owner ruled against), and an index-row summary replaced wholesale all pass lint clean, while an unresolvable reference inside the block and a deleted index row both fire. The lawfulness half is unreachable by any guard -- whether cited evidence truly falsifies a sentence is judgment -- and that half is not what this records; the marker-block biconditional is mechanical and uncovered. Not fixed: zero instances exist in 48 entries, the change itself records that the clause landed with no live customer, and the remedy would be the first guard to read entry body structure, with a false-positive class (any bracketed 'corrected' written for another reason) that would red lawful work.
promotion: the first erratum landing footer-only or marker-only in a real entry.

artifact: skills/adversarial-review/SKILL.md:41 -- the load-bearing-claim standard, as applied to universals
finding: Two seats independently sustained the same unchecked universal in one review -- 'the ## References section every entry ends with' / 'every entry carries', true 1 time in 48, and the one entry carrying it was the artifact under review. A third seat miscounted the same file's skills/ citations as thirteen against an actual fifteen. Each was caught downstream and none changed a disposition. The lens is already worded at :41 ('Load hides in absence claims, universals, superlatives, and counts -- check those first'), so this is under-application rather than a gap, and a promoted lens restating it would be the armor authoring bars.
promotion: a second review where a seat files on an unchecked universal or count.

artifact: skills/adversarial-review/SKILL.md -- the session note's rank over behaviour
finding: A seat cited the experience-session note as independently corroborating its finding that one README sentence gives two opposite answers about whether a correction changes a claim. The note reports no such friction: its reported difficulty is bound three's description-versus-judgment line, a different sentence carried by a different finding. The standards give a note rank 'on behavior and on nothing else', so citing it for a claim it does not report carries that rank onto an unprobed claim -- and the claim it was lent to was then disproved by the defense and dropped by the judge.
promotion: a second instance of a session note cited for a claim it does not report.

artifact: skills/adversarial-review/SKILL.md:41 -- the load-bearing-claim standard, as applied to counts
finding: A fourth instance of a stated count reaching a stage unchecked, in the same review. The post-fix look wrote '17 of 48 entries carry a pin; 28 pinned references against 14 unpinned' in a declined examination. Re-derived at 4e2bc92 by the terminal stage: 48 entries, 12 carrying a pinned reference under lint._entry_refs, 28 path-form pinned against 199 path-form unpinned, 29 against 299 overall -- 14 reproduces under no basis, being figures.py's unresolvable-reference census, a different quantity. The class is covered twice over, since authoring's figure rule independently binds a derived figure on a seat report to its command, and is still skipped -- so the failure is not that a rule is missing or unclear. Round one's own promoter was not met on its terms: it named a second review where a seat files, and this is the same review's second cycle, in a declined examination on which no disposition turned.
promotion: a stated count a later stage cannot reproduce where a review's ruling actually turned on it, or a mechanism proposed that could check a count over a corpus the change itself writes into.

artifact: tools/lint.py -- the repository-wide walks: _iter_files, _python_files, and _prose_files
finding: _prose_files is a third rglob of the whole repository, differing from _iter_files only by a .git clause, and its docstring described its provenance as check_emitted_ascii's walk, which is narrower (*.py rather than *). The remedy is determined -- one shared walk, or git ls-files -co --exclude-standard, which returns tracked plus untracked-not-ignored in a single call and removes the check-ignore round trip too -- but the walk was measured at 4ms of a 0.88s run, so the cost case for acting is absent and the duplication is the whole of the harm. The docstring sentences were corrected; the third copy was left standing.
promotion: a fourth repository-wide walk is written, or a filter has to be applied across all of them at once, or a walk's cost is measured as a material share of a lint run.

artifact: tools/roster.py -- frontmatter()'s paragraph on the interior line endings it copies
finding: The sentence 'the committed bytes are the same wherever the generator last ran' is stated without the bound in_step states two functions down: git's text=auto refuses to normalise a file holding a lone carriage return, so a cell carrying one inside its frontmatter propagates it into the entry verbatim. Probed: such a cell and its entry both commit as i/-text. The only remedy adds a clause to the paragraph an experience session established, from real use, is the one a cold consumer reads and is turned by -- the consumer arrived with the wrong thesis and that paragraph corrected it -- and the bound is already stated in full, in the function whose job it is. Weight against a reader nobody has observed failing.
promotion: a session reuses frontmatter() outside the roster generator, or a report that a reader acted wrongly on the unqualified sentence, or the bound stops being stated on in_step.

artifact: tools/lint.py -- the message class for findings about the lint itself, being check-raised and check_emitted_ascii's unparseable-file branch
finding: check-raised states the situation and names no next step, so a session holding a red on the flow's mandated pre-commit gate is not told whether to file, re-run, or proceed. The claim that it is the only such message in the file was disproved: emitted-ascii's unparseable branch does the same, and is the same kind of message -- a report that the lint could not do its job rather than a report about the tree -- so check-raised follows a house pattern rather than breaking one. The remedy adds prose to a message an experience session established is untested by use, and if bought it covers both messages or neither.
promotion: a session reports being unable to act on a check-raised or unparseable-file finding, or a third message of this class is written, or either message is observed in use.

artifact: tools/lint.py -- check_committed_carriage_return's binary test
finding: The check skips binary content on a NUL in the first 8000 bytes, matched to git's own detection window so the two cannot disagree inside it. A binary whose first NUL falls past 8000 still classifies as i/-text, still has its bytes read, and still draws a finding whose remedy a reader cannot safely apply. The class is unclosable at this layer: git's own classification cannot separate such a file from a lone-carriage-return text file, which is the thing the check exists for. The remedy clause was softened to stop instructing a rewrite unconditionally; the misfire itself stands.
promotion: the first binary is tracked in this repository, or a finding is reported against a file whose text-ness the check cannot establish.

artifact: tools/lint.py -- _read_text's None, and what a check does with a file it cannot read
finding: _read_text returns None for 'binary, deliberately out of scope' and for 'could not be read' alike, so a caller cannot tell them apart and the mandated command can exit 0 over content it never examined -- the shape check_emitted_ascii's own message condemns. Distinguishing them changes a helper's contract with four consumers, which is a design call, and the docstring names two siblings (roster.is_generated, _git_ignored) that answer silently by design. The raising half was fixed; this is the silent half.
promotion: a third caller needs to tell the two apart, or a run is reported clean over content it could not read.

artifact: tools/lint.py -- check_committed_carriage_return's message for the untracked population
finding: The finding class is named committed-carriage-return and its remedy says to stage the file, but the untracked population reaches files a session may never intend to commit: persist.py stages only named pathspecs, so an untracked non-ignored scratch file is not on its way to a commit. The remedy adds a conditional clause to a message that two consecutive experience sessions establish is untested by use, which is the reasoning round one used to record the sibling finding about check-raised. A gitignored scratch file is already excluded, so the class is narrow.
promotion: a session reports being told to stage a file it did not intend to commit, or any untracked-population finding is observed in use.

artifact: tools/lint.py -- the skip lists, FROZEN_ARCHIVE and LIVE_RECORDS, against AGENTS.md
finding: The lists restate what the doctrine names rather than deriving from it, so a frozen path added to AGENTS.md and omitted here passes every test. Deriving them from the doctrine is the real remedy and was priced as bigger than the defect it closes. The test that claimed to check the lists against the prose now pins what they hold instead, which is the narrower true thing.
promotion: a frozen path is added to AGENTS.md, or a third list of doctrine-named paths is written into a tool.

artifact: tools/lint.py -- BODY_STRIP_RECORDED and its suite pin
finding: The set has no ratchet. Two invented exemptions pass silently and nothing reports an entry that has gone stale; the pin is an equality assertion against a literal, so adding an exemption to clear a red is a two-line edit. What the pin buys is visibility in a diff, not prevention -- the comment, the entry and the test docstring were corrected to say so. The real remedy is a stale-exemption report on check_entry_references' model, ~15 lines plus tests, declined because the batch's own predicate fix shrank the set rather than growing it, so the evidence that exemption creep is real is absent.
promotion: BODY_STRIP_RECORDED grows, or an entry in it goes stale.

artifact: AGENTS.md 'Content routing, here' -- the rule-versus-document discriminator
finding: The binding-docs/ bullet makes the bullet above it non-exhaustive, and the only discriminator is 'rule or mechanic' against 'document', which the surface never defines. Read as an escape, any rule could be exported to docs/ behind a one-line pointer instead of spending its own characters here, which removes the displacement pressure the budget exists to apply. The meaning change is recorded in D-253; defining the discriminator on the surface was declined because it costs characters this surface does not have and the escape is an unprobed behaviour claim.
promotion: a rule is routed to docs/ to avoid spending AGENTS.md characters.

artifact: tools/lint.py -- check_body_strip_owner's BODY_STRIP_OWNER exemption
finding: The owner is exempt as a whole file, so a second hand-rolled strip added to skills/authoring/scripts/figures.py -- the module most likely to attract one -- is guarded by nothing, and BODY_STRIP_OWNER is not covered by the membership pin either. Keying it as (path, qualified name) is a few lines, but the engine may legitimately hold helpers and deciding which of its names are lawful is a design call. The false claim was the live defect and is fixed: the check now states the exemption is wholesale and why.
promotion: a second hand-rolled strip lands in the authoring engine.

artifact: AGENTS.md -- 'Shared code lives only in lib/' against the body-strip guard's remedy
finding: The guard's remedy mandates importing skills/authoring/scripts/figures.py, which is shared code outside lib/, and the doctrine sentence says shared code lives only in lib/. Two experience-session consumers reported no doubt about the import permission, so nothing observed is blocked by it; closing the inaccuracy costs AGENTS.md characters against a surface at its ceiling. The missing half is the resolution *route* rather than the permission, and that is #241's, which the affirmed boundary parked.
promotion: a session reads 'only in lib/' and declines a lawful cell-scripts/ import.

artifact: skills/authoring/SKILL.md and references/routing.md -- the genuinely exhausted surface
finding: A refusal discharges the outflow obligation but frees no characters, and the budget check is a hard finding, so at an exhausted surface the lint stays red while the cell's new sentence forbids the two remaining moves (shrink the addition, decline the edit) and names no next action. Four budgeted surfaces are near their ceilings, the charter's body the tightest -- python tools/figures.py prices them all. The next action is written down only in tools/lint.py's budget-constant comments, which is the class this change exists to close. The only remedy is more prose on a cell already at its own ceiling, so it would trigger its own outflow; no surface is over budget yet.
promotion: a budgeted surface goes over and the three moves cannot clear it.

artifact: tools/lint.py -- the recorded remedy for check_subprocess_streams' repository-root walk
finding: check_body_strip_owner is a third site of the SHIPPED_DIRS + REPO_ONLY_NAMES walk, so it shares both recorded blind spots: a repository-root .py file is never read, and the walk does not filter through .gitignore. Neither promotion condition has fired and reusing _iter_files is not a fourth walk helper, so neither recorded finding is promoted -- three review seats independently reached that same decline. What is new is the price: the recorded remedy 'widen the walk' now diverges two checks' walks rather than one.
promotion: a fourth site of this walk shape is written, or either sibling finding is promoted and the widening has to cover both.

artifact: tools/check_version_bump.py -- the untracked-file enumeration on a tree without .gitignore
finding: The guard enumerates untracked files with git ls-files --others --exclude-standard, which honours .gitignore. On a tree that has none, running the suite the flow mandates immediately beforehand creates __pycache__ under skills/ and lib/, and the guard reads them as a shipped-zone change and demands a plugin version bump; running the guard alone regenerates lib/__pycache__ and reddens on the artifact its own execution just created. The message is confident and specific and gives no hint the files are build artifacts, so the likely resolution is a version bump shipped for a repo-only change. No live instance here -- this repository tracks .gitignore and the guard reports one shipped file. Observed by an experience-session consumer against a tree whose isolation had dropped the file, which is how the class surfaced at all.
promotion: an adopting repository reports a version bump made to clear a red naming build artifacts, or a tree here loses its .gitignore.
